ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p577#3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p577#3/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p577#3/r4.claim: Lafḥ is the scorching impact of fire's heat; al-Zajjāj says it has a stronger effect than laqīḥ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p577#3/r4.anchor: اللفح: إصابة النار الشيء بوهجها وإحراقها. وقال الزجاج: اللفح أشد من اللقيح تأثيرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p577#3/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p577#3/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p577#3/r5.claim: Kulūḥ is lips pulling back from the teeth, like a dog's or lion's grimace; another explanation is a frowning, contorted face, with several related word forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p577#3/r5.anchor: الكلوح: تشمر الشفتين عن الأسنان ومنه كلوح كلوح الكلب والأسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r9.claim: The face is singled out because it is the person's most honored and protected part; if fire scorches it, the lesser parts are scorched too, leading into the description of grimacing lips.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p584/r9.anchor: وخص الوجه باللفح لأنه أشرف ما في الإنسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhī records that the upper lip contracts to the middle of the head and the lower lip hangs to the navel; he grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r1.anchor: وفي الترمذي تتقلص شفته العليا حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r2.speaker: أبو حيوة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r2.claim: Abū Ḥaywah, Abū Baḥriyya, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read “kāliḥūn” without the alif.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p585/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وأبو بحرية وابن أبي عبلة كلحون بغير ألف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r3.claim: Talfah means the fire scorches or burns their faces; kāliḥūn means frowning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r3.anchor: تلفح وجوههم النار} أي: تسفع، وقيل: تحرق، {وهم فيها كالحون} عابسون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r4.claim: The Prophet describes the fire drawing the upper lip to the head’s middle and loosening the lower lip to the navel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r4.anchor: فتقلص شفته العليا حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه، وتسترخي شفته السفلى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r5.claim: The disbeliever grows to the size of a seven-night journey in the Fire, with a molar like Mount Uḥud and lips at the navel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r5.anchor: يعظم الكافر في النار مسيرة سبع ليال

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r3.claim: The fire burns their faces severely; their pursed lips pull away from their teeth, and the verb may be read with a light or doubled consonant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:103-106/r3.anchor: تحرقها واللفح كالنفح إلا أنه أشد تأثيرا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r7.claim: The fire scorches faces with intense heat; the damned are disfigured, their lips drawn back over their teeth in grim anguish.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r7.anchor: أي متقلصو الشفاه عن الأسنان مع عبوسة الوحوه وتجعدها وتقطبها

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the Fire’s action, talfaḥ, with tanqaḥ.
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس {تلفح وجوههم النار} قال تنقح

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r7.claim: The Prophet says a blast of fire makes their flesh flow down onto their nerves.
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r7.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله {تلفح وجوههم النار} قال: تلفحهم لفحة فتسيل لحومهم

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r8.claim: Hell meets those driven to it with its neck and blasts them, leaving no flesh on the bones except what falls to the ankles.
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن جهنم لما سيق إليها أهلها تلقتهم بعنق فلفحتهم لفحة

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the blast strips flesh from the bones and casts it onto the heels; Abu al-Hudhayl reports the same.
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {تلفح وجوههم النار} قال: لفحتهم لفحة فما أبقت لحما على عظم

DURR-FULL:v6p117/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r10.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r10.claim: The Prophet says the Fire disfigures faces: the upper lip shrinks to mid-head while the lower lip hangs to the navel.
DURR-FULL:v6p117/r10.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله {تلفح وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون} قال تشويه النار فتقلص شفته العليا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r3.claim: Lafh means the fire's scorching heat; Abu Haywa's kalihun without alif describes lips drawn back to expose teeth, like singed rams' heads.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156#2/r3.anchor: و «لفح النار» إصابتها بالوهج والإحراق، وقرأ أبو حيوة «كلحون» بغير ألف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r3.claim: Talfaḥ means to scorch or sear.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says lafḥ and nafḥ are alike, except lafḥ has a stronger effect.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج : اللفح والنفح واحد ، إلا أن اللفح أشد تأثيرا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r5.claim: Kuluḥ is the lips retracting from the teeth, like the heads of roasted animals.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r5.anchor: والكلوح : أن تتقلص الشفتان وتتشمرا عن الأسنان ، كما ترى الرؤوس المشوية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r6.speaker: مالك بن دينار
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r6.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says seeing a head taken from an oven in the market caused ʿUtba al-Ghulam’s repentance and left him unconscious for three days.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r6.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار : كان سبب توبة عتبة الغلام أنه مر في السوق برأس أخرج من التنور

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r7.claim: A report describes Hell retracting the upper lip to the middle of the head and dropping the lower lip to the navel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r7.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r8.claim: A reading has “they are scorched,” with the alternative form kulihun.

MUQATIL:23:101-105/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r4.claim: Talfaḥ means to blow; those in Hell are grimacing, with upper lips raised, teeth exposed, and lower lips striking their bellies.
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r4.anchor: { تلفح } يعنى تنفخ { وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون } [آية: 104] عابسين شفته العليا قالصة لا تغطى أنيابه،

MUQATIL:23:101-105/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r5.claim: Their teeth protrude forty cubits, measured by the stature of the first creation, and each canine is like Mount Uhud.
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r5.anchor: وهم فيها كالحون } [آية: 104] عابسين شفته العليا قالصة لا تغطى أنيابه، وشفته السفلى تضرب بطنه، وثناياه خارجة من فيه بين شفتيه أربعون ذراعا،

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the fire's striking as hitting and consuming faces' flesh and skin.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أي تضرب وتأكل لحومهم وجلودهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r13.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r13.claim: Al-Zajjaj says lafḥ and nafḥ both mean a blast, but lafḥ has a stronger effect.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r13.anchor: قال الزجاج : اللفح والنفخ واحد إلا أن اللفح أشد تأثيرا

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r14.claim: Kāliḥ means the lips retract and pull apart from the teeth, like the heads of roasted animals.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r14.anchor: والكلوح أن تتقلص الشفتان ويتباعدا عن الأسنان

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r15.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r15.claim: The Prophet describes the upper lip shrinking to the middle of the head and the lower lip drooping to the navel.
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r15.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r16.anchor: وقرىء ( كلحون ) ، ثم إنه سبحانه لما شرح عذابهم

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.claim: The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.anchor: will desire to go back to the world in order to do good instead of evil, though it will be too late for them (vv.99–118)

TAB-FULL:v17p115/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r2.claim: The fire burns and scorches their faces; their lips contract away from their teeth, leaving the teeth exposed.
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r2.anchor: والكلوح: أن تتقلص الشفتان عن الأسنان حتى تبدو الأسنان

TAB-FULL:v17p115/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “the fire strikes their faces” as “it blows upon them,” and describes the damned as frowning.
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {تلفح وجوههم النار} [المؤمنون: 104] قال: «تنفح»

TAB-FULL:v17p115/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r4.speaker: الأعشى
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r4.claim: Al-Aʿshā's poetic line uses “kalih” for a mouth whose lips draw back from the canine tooth, supporting the gloss of contracted lips.
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r4.anchor: كما قال الأعشى: [البحر الرمل] وله المقدم لا مثل له … ساعة الشدق عن الناب كلح

TAB-FULL:v17p115/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r5.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r5.claim: ʿAbd Allāh compares the damned to a fire-scorched head with exposed teeth and contracted lips.
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r5.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص، عن عبد الله، في قوله: {وهم فيها كالحون} [المؤمنون: 104] قال: «ألم تر إلى الرأس المشيط

TAB-FULL:v17p115/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd compares their faces to sheep's faces when touched by fire.
TAB-FULL:v17p115/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وهم فيها كالحون}

TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r2.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r2.claim: Lafh and nafh both describe heat striking the face, but lafh is stronger, like a scorching poisonous blast; nafh is a breeze touching the face.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r2.anchor: إلا أن اللفح أشد تأثيرا وأعظم من النفح

TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r3.speaker: مجمع البيان
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r3.claim: Kuluḥ is the lips contracting away from the teeth until the teeth show.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r3.anchor: والكلوح تقلص الشفتين عن الأسنان حتى تبدو الأسنان

TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r4.claim: The fire makes the lips contract and the teeth show, leaving faces like roasted heads.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#2/r4.anchor: يصيب وجوههم لهب النار حتى تتقلص شفاههم وتنكشف عن أسنانهم كالرؤوس المشوية

TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r4.claim: Al-Qummi explains that the fire blazes over and burns their faces, while their grimacing means open mouths and darkened faces.
TABATABAI:23:99-118#6/r4.anchor: قال تلهب عليهم فتحرقهم { وهم فيها كالحون }

TABRISI:23:101/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101/r4.claim: Lafḥ and nafḥ both mean a scorching touch, but lafḥ has a stronger and more severe effect on the face.
TABRISI:23:101/r4.anchor: اللفح والنفح بمعنى إلا أن اللفح أشد تأثيرا وأعظم من النفح

TABRISI:23:101/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101/r5.claim: Kuluḥ is the lips drawing back from the teeth until the teeth show; al-Aʿshā’s verse illustrates the word kalih.
TABRISI:23:101/r5.anchor: والكلوح تقلص الشفتين عن الأسنان حتى تبدو الأسنان قال الأعشى

TABRISI:23:101/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101/r8.claim: Talfaḥu wujūhahum is an accusative circumstantial clause, with khālidūn as its governor.
TABRISI:23:101/r8.anchor: تلفح وجوههم النار في موضع النصب على الحال والعامل فيه خالدون

TABRISI:23:101-108/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101-108/r11.claim: The fire’s flames strike their faces; kalih describes a grimacing expression, and Ibn Abbas glosses it as frowning.
TABRISI:23:101-108/r11.anchor: أي يصيب وجوههم لفح النار ولهبها

TABRISI:23:101-108/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r12.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:23:101-108/r12.claim: Hasan describes the damned as lips contracted until their teeth show, like roasted heads.
TABRISI:23:101-108/r12.anchor: هو أن تتقلص شفاههم وتبدو أسنانهم كالرؤوس المشوية عن الحسن

THALABI:v7p57/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p57/r4.claim: He glosses تلفح as scorching the faces.

THALABI:v7p57/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p57/r5.claim: كالحون describes grimacing; another explanation is that the lips retract until the teeth appear.
THALABI:v7p57/r5.anchor: عابسون عن ابن عباس، وقال غيره: الكلوح أن تتقلص الشفتان عن الإنسان حتى تبدو الأسنان

THALABI:v7p57/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
THALABI:v7p57/r6.claim: He describes a head scorched by fire with exposed teeth and contracted lips.

THALABI:v7p57/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r7.speaker: الأعشى
THALABI:v7p57/r7.claim: His verse uses كلح for a mouth or cheek drawn back so the tooth is exposed.

THALABI:v7p57/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v7p57/r8.claim: The Prophet says the Fire shrivels the upper lip to the middle of the head and makes the lower lip hang to the navel.
THALABI:v7p57/r8.anchor: تشويه النار فتتقلص شفته العليا حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r3.claim: Yaḥyā says he received from Ibn Masʿūd a comparison of the damned person's face to a singed head.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r3.anchor: قال يحيى: وبلغني عن ابن مسعود قال: مثل الرأس المشيط.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the lower lip hangs to the chest while the upper curls and covers the face.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله: «شفته السفلى ساقطة على صدره،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r5.claim: Another report says a disbeliever grows as tall as seven nights and with molars like Mount Uḥud, with swollen dark-blue lips; Hell asks whether it is full until God places His foot in it.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r5.anchor: حاجب بن عمر، عن عمه الحكم بن الأعرج، عن أبي هريرة قال: يعظم الكافر في النار مسيرة سبع ليال، ضرسه مثل أحد

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.claim: Salvation depends on the amount of reward earned through faith and good works: those whose deeds weigh heavily succeed, while those whose scales are light suffer loss and enter enduring Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.anchor: tartıları yani sevapları ağır basanlar kurtuluşa erecek, tartıları hafif kalanlar da derin bir hüsrana uğrayacak, ebedî ve dehşetli bir azap sürecini yaşamak üzere cehenneme atılacaklardır.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r1.claim: Only deeds will matter on Judgment Day; relationships will not avail anyone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p283/r1.anchor: On that day, only deeds – and not relationships – will be any avail.

BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r1.claim: Lafḥ means that fire burns with its heat; al-Qāmūs glosses it as burning, and al-Irshād says it is more forceful than nafḥ.
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r1.anchor: {تلفح وجوههم النار} تحرقها يقال : لفحته النار بحرها أحرقته

BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r2.claim: Faces are singled out as the noblest and most protected members, making their punishment a stronger deterrent; they precede the agent in the wording.
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r2.anchor: وتخصيص الوجوه بذلك لأنها أشرف الأعضاء وأعظم ما يصان منها فبيان حالها أزجر عن المعاصي المؤدية إلى النار

BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r3.claim: Kāliḥūn means their lips shrink back from their teeth in the intense burning, like roasted heads.
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r3.anchor: والكلوح تقلص الشفتين عن الأسنان كما ترى الرؤوس المشوية

BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r4.speaker: مالك بن دينار
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r4.claim: Mālik ibn Dīnār says ʿUtba the young ascetic repented after seeing a head taken from an oven; he fainted for three days and nights.
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r4.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار كان سبب توبة عتبة الغلام أنه مر في السوق برأس أخرج من التنور

BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r5.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r5.claim: A hadith describes the fire drawing the upper lip to the middle of the head and letting the lower lip hang to the navel.
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث : "تشويه النار فتقلص شفته العليا حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه

BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r6.claim: The condemned are addressed by way of reproach, rebuke, and reminding them why they deserved the punishment they suffer.
BURSEVI:v6p77#2/r6.anchor: فيقال لهم تعنيفا وتوبيخا وتذكيرا لما به استحقوا ما ابتلوا به من العذاب

STUDYQURAN:23:104/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:104/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:104/r1.claim: The verb rendered smite can also mean burn or scorch.
STUDYQURAN:23:104/r1.anchor: Smite renders a verb that also means “to burn or scorch.”

STUDYQURAN:23:104/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:104/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:104/r2.claim: Other passages describe the Fire or punishment appearing on human faces.
STUDYQURAN:23:104/r2.anchor: Other verses that contain a description of the Fire

STUDYQURAN:23:104/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:104/r3.speaker: some commentators (Q, Ṭ)
STUDYQURAN:23:104/r3.claim: Some explain the grimace as the flames disfiguring the lips.
STUDYQURAN:23:104/r3.anchor: According to some commentators, the grimace results from the disfigurement of the lips by the flames (Q, Ṭ).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r1.claim: Lafḥ means burning; fire or the hot sirocco is said to burn someone.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r2.claim: Talfaḥ and tanfaḥ have the same basic meaning, but talfaḥ has the stronger effect.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r2.anchor: وقال الزجاج: تلفح وتنفح بمعنى واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r3.claim: Kulūḥ is exposing the teeth while scowling; related usage describes severe weather.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r4.claim: A kāliḥ has lips drawn back from the teeth, like a sheep's head with its teeth showing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الكالح: الذي قد شمرت شفتاه عن أسنانه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd likens it to a head scorched by fire, its teeth showing and lips contracted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن مسعود -في هذه الآية-: ألم تر إلى الرأس المشيط

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r6.speaker: الخدري عن رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r6.claim: The Prophet says the fire pulls the upper lip to the middle of the head and the lower lip to the navel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70#2/r6.anchor: وروى الخدري، عن رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- في هذه الآية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r1.anchor: { تلفح } تحرق. { وهم فيها كالحون } عابسون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r2.claim: They grimace because the burning contracts their lips.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:104-106/r2.anchor: وهم فيها كالحون } عابسون لتقلص شفاههم

ITQAN:v4p522#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p522#4/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p522#4/r1.claim: A report says the Prophet told a man he would die at al-Rabwa, but he died at al-Ramla; Ibn Kathīr calls the report very unusual.
ITQAN:v4p522#4/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن مرة البهزي قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول لرجل

ITQAN:v4p522#4/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p522#4/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p522#4/r4.claim: Abū Saʿīd reports that the Fire disfigures the damned: the upper lip retracts to the head’s midpoint and the lower lip sags to the navel.
ITQAN:v4p522#4/r4.anchor: وأخرج أحمد والترمذي عن أبي سعيد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r1.claim: Talfaḥu may begin an independent sentence, function circumstantially, or serve as another predicate of ulāʾika.
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r1.anchor: يجوز استئنافه، ويجوز حاليته. ويجوز كونه

SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r2.claim: Lafḥ is the fire striking, scorching, and burning something, more severe than nafḥ.
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r2.anchor: إصابة النار الشيء/ وكلحها وإحراقها له

SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r3.claim: Kulūḥ is the upper lip drawn up and the lower lip slackened; the cited al-Tirmidhī report describes them stretching to the head’s middle and navel.
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r3.anchor: وفي الترمذي: تتقلص شفته العليا، حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه، وتسترخي السفلى حتى تبلغ سرته

SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r4.claim: The expression “a lion’s kulūḥ” denotes baring its teeth; a harsh day or cold is also called kāliḥ.
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r4.anchor: أي: تكشيره عن أنيابه. ودهر كالح، وبرد كالح

SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r5.claim: Another explanation takes kulūḥ as a frowning, grimacing face.
SAMIN-DURR:23:104/r5.anchor: وقيل: الكلوح هو: تقطيب الوجه وبسوره

ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r2.claim: Lafḥ and nafaḥ have similar meanings, but lafḥ has the stronger effect.
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r2.anchor: يلفح وينفح في معنى واحد، إلا أن اللفح أعظم تأثيرا

ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r3.claim: A kalih has lips drawn back from the teeth, like sheep's heads when fire exposes their teeth and shrivels their lips.
ZAJJAJ:v4p23/r3.anchor: والكالح الذي قد تشمرت شفته عن أسنانه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#4/r1.speaker: عبد الله ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#4/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd illustrates the scorched, grimacing face by describing a head singed by fire, with lips torn away and teeth exposed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#4/r1.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص أن عبد الله ابن مسعود قرأ الآية ﴿ تلفح وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون ﴾ قال ألم تر إلى الرأس المشيط بالنار

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r1.claim: The clause about the fire scorching their faces is either circumstantial or a new sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r1.anchor: جملة حالية أو مستأنفة واللفح مس لهب النار الشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r2.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r2.claim: Lafh is flame contact; al-Zajjaj says it is more intense than nafh, and here it means the fire burns their faces.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r2.anchor: واللفح مس لهب النار الشيء وهو كما قال الزجاج أشد من النفح تأثيرا والمراد تحرق وجوههم النار

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r3.claim: Faces are singled out because they are the noblest limbs and their punishment is more deterrent, explaining their precedence before fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r3.anchor: وتخصيص الوجوه بذلك لأنها أشرف الأعضاء فبيان حالها أزجر عن المعاصي المؤدية إلى النار

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r4.claim: The condemned grimace, with their lips drawn back from their teeth by the scorching.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r4.anchor: متقلصو الشفاه عن الأسنان من أثر ذلك اللفح

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r5.claim: A sound report from the Prophet says the fire disfigures them: the upper lip retracts to mid-head and the lower lip sags to the navel.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r5.anchor: أنه قال في الآية تشويه النار فتقلص شفته العليا حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r6.claim: A report from the Prophet says one blast scorches them and their flesh runs down to their heels.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r6.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله تعالى ( تلفح ) الخ : تلفحهم لفحة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses grimacing as the face being ugly and contorted.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r7.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن الكلوح بسور الوجه وتقطيبه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r8.speaker: أبو حيوة وأبو بحرية وابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r8.claim: These readers pronounce the word without the alif, as the plural of kalih.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#4/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وأبو بحرية وابن أبي عبلة ( كلحون ) بغير ألف جمع كلح كحذر

DURR-FULL:v6p118/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r1.speaker: مغيث بن سمي
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r1.claim: Mughith describes a man brought to the Fire and given a cup of snake venom that makes flesh and bone separate as it nears his mouth.
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r1.anchor: عن مغيث بن سمي قال: إذا جيء بالرجل إلى النار قيل انتظر حتى تنحفك فيؤتى بكأس من سم الأفاعي

DURR-FULL:v6p118/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r2.claim: Ibn Masud likens their grimace to a roasted head: their teeth show and their lips contract.
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود في قوله {وهم فيها كالحون} قال: كلوح الرأس النضيج بدت أسنانهم وتقلصت شفاههم

DURR-FULL:v6p118/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses their condition as frowning.
DURR-FULL:v6p118/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {كالحون} قال: عابسون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127/r1.claim: The clause about the fire striking their faces is circumstantial to those who lost themselves; talfaḥ means to burn, with the sense of a severe impact from fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127/r1.anchor: وجملة { تلفح وجوههم النار } في موضع الحال من { الذين خسروا أنفسهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127/r2.claim: A kāliḥ is someone whose lips contract and teeth show as facial nerves tighten from severe pain.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p127/r2.anchor: والكالح : الذي به الكلوح وهو تقلص الشفتين وظهور الأسنان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says talfaḥ and tanfaḥ have the same basic meaning, but talfaḥ has the more severe effect.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج تلفح وتنفح بمعنى واحد إلا أن اللفح أعظم تأثيرا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r2.claim: Kāliḥ describes lips pulled back from the teeth, like sheep's heads with teeth exposed and lips contracted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r2.anchor: والكالح الذي قد تشمرت شفته عن اسنانه نحو ما ترى من رؤوس الغنم إذا برزت الأسنان وتشمرت الشفاه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd describes their teeth as showing and their lips contracted like a head scorched by fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود قد بدت أسنانهم وتقلصت شفاههم كالرأس المشيط بالنار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r4.claim: Al-Ḥākim includes in his Ṣaḥīḥ a report from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī from the Prophet: fire disfigures them, drawing the upper lip to mid-head and the lower lip down to the navel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p491/r4.anchor: وروى أبو عبد الله الحاكم في صحيحه من حديث أبي سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في هذه الآية تشويه النار فتقلص شفته العليا حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497/r1.claim: The Fire scorches their faces, as also described in 14:50 and 21:39.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497/r2.claim: The Prophet reports that when Hell's people are driven to it, its flame meets and scorches them so fiercely that their flesh falls away except at the ankles.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن جهنم لما سيق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains kāliḥūn as people with grimacing, frowning faces.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd likens them to a scorched head with exposed teeth and contracted lips.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r2.anchor: وقال الثوري، عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي الأحوص، عن عبد الله بن مسعود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says the Fire disfigures them: the upper lip contracts to midhead and the lower lip droops to the navel; al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p497#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: {وهم فيها كالحون}

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#4/r2.claim: Kalihun means grimacing or frowning; the verse continues by saying that something is said to them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ وجوههم النار وهم فيها كالحون ﴾ عابسون فيقال لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r1.claim: Tanfahu is a synonym of talfahu, as in 21:46, but talfahu conveys more intense torment; fire or scorching wind burns, while a sword’s lafḥa is a light blow.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses kāliḥūn as scowling; lexicographers describe the grimace as baring teeth with the lips drawn back.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: عابسون. وقال أهل اللغة: الكلوح تكشر في عبوس

QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r3.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r3.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line uses kalaḥ for a mouth whose cheek draws back from the tooth at the moment of struggle.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r3.anchor: قال الأعشى: وله المقدم لا مثل له ساعة الشدق عن الناب كلح

QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r4.claim: Qurtubi notes forms kalaha, kulūḥan, and kalāḥan; kalḥa can mean the mouth and its surroundings, and a grim day is severe.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas also describes them as one whose lips contract and whose pus flows.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا «وهم فيها كالحون» يريد كالذي كلح وتقلصت شفتاه وسال صديده

QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd likens them to a scorched sheep’s head, with teeth exposed and lips contracted.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r6.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: ألم تر إلى رأس المشيط بالنار

QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r7.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports from the Prophet that fire shrinks the upper lip to mid-head and slackens the lower lip to the navel; al-Tirmidhī grades it ṣaḥīḥ gharīb.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:104-105/r7.anchor: وفي الترمذي عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال
